This Is Probably Crap, But It's An Idea.

Could I run a competition where you have to make a race out of the given tileset?
I was busy making it, then realised that millions of routes could be made, and someone was bound to make a better one out of it than me.

I would judge on:

/20 - Route (/10 - How original is the route? : /10 Is it too confusing?)
/20 - Flow (Is it too rough? Or as smooth as a baby's bum?)
/20 - Item Placement (Too cluttered? Too little?)
/20 - Difficulty (Is it too hard or easy to be fun?)
/20 - Length (Too long? Over in an instant?)

RULES:
No tiles editing.
Pre-given items, including Ninja, are only there as a guide, and can be deleted.
NaNified drones allowed, but only two teleporters per map.
One entry each, to avoid repetition.

JUDGES:
Would hopefully be me and two others, and a backup / judge's judge.


You can tell I wanna do this, can't you?
Please tell me if this would be good, or give me any hints to improve the idea.
Thanks.

#12436 1 2006-11-24T13:54:26Z Ad
(For Lostprophets, Go Down)

Muse:
IT CODGING RULED!

I'd never screamed so loud.

Anyway, from the beginning:

Thurs 23rd November '06 (Bare professional)
Met up with mates, bla bla, met some random 19 year old that made me feel like a giant. Shwoz 5foot1.
Tube Train chugs.
Exit Wembley Park Tube Station. Fall over Webley Stadium. It's around 200 metres away. Looks so cool.
Twaddle over to Wemblewy Arena, newly 100% LEDed. Got my ticket taken and got a pink flurescent wristband. Woo!
Enter, gasp at refuribish Wembley Arena, down a bottle of water, enter the floor.
Get forced to sit. Stand, go to piss. Twice. Curse my pathetic bladder control!
Buy gig top.
Over an hour and a half later, the support act, The Noisettes, appeared, who were actually pretty good. Though the music was repetitive, and the lead singer continued to squeal like a pig cut in half. But the most disturbing part of their 40 minute act was watching the insane drummers moobs almost hit him in the face several times over.

40 minutes.
Bet Khights will be starting act.

5 Minutes.
Crowd explodes. Curtain drops to reveal Matt in his orange tracksuit, Dom, mit freshly shaven head, and a giant upside down cone with a pixellated display on the outside, on stage right. Raised to reveal Dom on a podeum.

Cue Knights.
Crowd roars.
I'm instantly thrown back 5 metres, but still have a perfect view. Bouncing begins.
I've never heard so many people imitate a high pitched voice.
Moshing ensues.

Follows on Starlight. Everything displays stars. Chorus sends them into space travel screensaver

Butterflies & Hurricanes. Awesome. The piano is ace. Extended guitar solo live is always great.

Map Of The Problematique. Continual jumping has never been so fun. 'Lonliness be over' bubbled over in the bg.

Riff. I knew it, everyone stared at me whilst I imitated it. Not cool. All cos I'm too hardcore for them

City of Delusion. Whipped out an acoustic and played tremendously. Introduced us to Trumpet player Dan. Though trumpet failed to do the string parts (as it's a trumpet) and effects were appauling, it was still a great song live.

And then he grabbed his reflective Knights guitar, walked to stage right. Hit a note. Held it. Put it to giant amp. Screeched. Took it away. Pulled a funny face. Changed note. Did this 3 times, and on the fourth time, the correct 1st note was played. Wow. *Drools at thought* Who cares about the awesomeness of the song, the atmosphere of the crowd, that 30 seconds summed up the ghettoness of the night.

Gathered around Dom's lil stand facing him, played forced in. Was expecting a follow up of bliss, got Hysteria instead, which lived up to it's name.

Citizen Erased. Brilliant track, shows Beller's writing ability. And insane hopping and jumping across the stage whilst playing shows his athletic ability too.

Hoodoo. -gutar intro = /me . Buty piano variation we ace. Go me, the only person that knew the words! Had some fat guy starin at me for it...

Invincible. -chaos pad = /me all like 'WTF?!HAX' but he used the time with free hands to raise the audience's energy levels. Me? I didn't need it, I had energy tablets Go Dextrose!

Supermassive. So. Fudging. Kewl. RANDOM MARCHING NINJAS IN BG! Solo hade me crap me pants too.

Time is running out. Most energetic performance by rabble (bar Knights) which was hard to keep up with.

New Born. Holy schmokes. I lurved es. Just the piano performance, the bassline, it is all fab.

5 min flippin 'yeah we're gonna pretend it's ended' which wore me out the most.

Apocalypse Please. What can I say? The piano is beautiful.

Bliss. Random countdown timer on right. 5 down to 1, through the quiet beginning bit, then it went nuts. Images then shown in countdown timer really made you think.

Balloons! 6 giant balloons, about the size of 5 people, were released from nowhere, filled with silver paper, I gotta hit one! They refused to play until we popped the last one, which refused to for 3 minutes, frantic boos could be heard everytime the balloon was relaunched by people. But the popping was insane, crowd started a mosh pit with no music

Muscle Museum. I'd have preferred seeing Fillip or Sober, even Sunburn, but I knew that wouldn't happen. This one's too popular. Hell, twas still good.

'This one's dedicated to all you crazy people in the middle.' MEEEEEEEEEEEEEEEEE.
Stockholm Syndrone begins. Love the quietLOUDquiet even more live. The space invaders style display was trific. Been searching for it on the net. No success.

Take a bow. Great ending song. Chanting about government rocks socks.

And alas, 2 Museiful hours were over. Dang.
Wish they'd played Hyper Music or TSP. They are great crowd action songs.

ABRIDGED VERSION:

The Set

Scaffolding: One pillar running up the front, perdendicular to theis was one beam running across the top of the front of stage. An LED rope was draped over to make it look like a crane. One pillar running up the back right, and another beam, running across the top of the back of set. Rope LEDs joined the two horizontal beams.

Back was a giant screen, with brilliant animations on, which could go transparent/lucent as desried, with floodlights that changed colour behind, capable of moving vertically. Giant upside down cone (stage right) could raise up to the ceiling and halfway as desired, and had visual displays on. PIC FROM WED GIG! Strobe lighting, and various other beams rigged aboved set to shing on set and on audience. A section out to either side with a mofo amp on.

If you can't picture any of it, THIS should help a bit. Tis centre stage.

The Songs (If you CBA to read all that above)

Knights Of Cydonia
Starlight
Butterflies & Hurricanes
Map Of TEH Problematique
Riff
City Of Delusion
-Humping Of Amp-
Plug In Baby
Forced In
Hysteria
Citizen Erased
Hoodoo
Invincible
Supermassive Black Hole
Another Riff
New Born

-Encore-

Apocalypse Please
Bliss

-Balloon Popping-

Muscle Museum
Stockholm Syndrome
Take A Bow

#259401 11 2006-11-25T10:27:48Z Ad
Lostprophets - Reading Rivermead... Sports Hall?!

Friday 24th November
Meet up with my mate Chris. Head off to this place. Completely shocked by the size of the place. And what it was. A sports hall! Twas funny. But yeh, took so long to get throo the door I missed the name of the first support, and they were pretty good. But Bring me the Horizon were balls, I don't care if they were British, they were BALLS. Hell, it may have been good if they had lyrics. Even Slipknot has lyrics. This was just 100%:
HHHHHHUUUUUUUUUUUUUUURRRRRRRRRRRGGGGGGGGHHGHHGHHHHHHHGAAARR.
Oh dear.

Was also surprised by the amount of diddy lil emo kids in there, that weren't over 12. And some random lil ten year olds! Was so confused. I didn't care, it meant I had a great view

Sooner or later, no wait, long time later, LP finally reared they Welsh backsides, and put on a hell of a performance. Started with A New Transmission, understandable. They've improved so much since I saw them supporting Linkin Park on their Meteora Tour ('03).

We got treated to a variety of class tracks, such as: (in no order, I've forgotten )

Can't Catch Tomorrow
4am Forever
Sway
Rooftops
Town Called Hypocracy
Last Summer
To Hell WeRide
We Still Kill The Old Way
Everyday Combat
Last Train Home

And then he asked us if anyone was at Reading '04 when they nearly killed 60000 people? Shinobi.

Instantly, a giant circle formed. I got to see everything, I was on the edge of it. About 50 people then went crazy whilst everyone watched on in awe.
But it wasn't over. Burn Burn began. The circle reopened to double, triple the size, and everyone went nuts. We reached the middle of the song, the band continued playing, but Ian gave us a 2 minute pep talk, saying how he wanted the fucking place to explode. And it did. The mosh pit was largened once again, and every one inside began lining the outside of it. As Ian began to sing the quiet Burn Burn chant style lyrics, everyone, including me, who was shovved in by some giant man who wanted to join in himself, started pacing round the inside. I was so lucky I got out before the screaming lyrics began. I'd have died. Twas completely nuts. Ian is a great ringleader.


I won't compare the two concoerts, it'd be pointless, just about everything that could possibly be different between the two concerts was different. But I will say one thing, when deciding between who to buy tickets for, Muse or Lostprophets, whatever choice you make is a stupid decision. Get both.

Amen.

Code green[/color]: Simple and fun. Not even a challenge, whatsoever, to any experienced player. Heck, even beginners wouldn't have any trouble beating it. This map would be like one you'd find in the first column on N.
Code yellow[/color]: Moderate difficulty. A bit of a challenge. Experts might beat it first try. Novices would require quite a few replays. The gold may present an optional challenge for skilled players. This map would be like one you'd find in one of the middle columns on N, like the 40's or 50's.
Code red[/color]: High difficulty. Even the experts would need a few gos at this map to get it right. Novices need not apply. All-golding the map would be an unrivaled feat of heroism. MTI would be a high-end code red map, as well as a few of the maps in the 80's and 90's column.

Hybrids. A lot of them have been seeing these parts recently.
Action/Puzzles

- Only two map types may be merged. But don't fret! I'm not limiting you to the normal level styles!

DDA

N-Art LINK (But seriously, if you don't know what a flipping NArt is...)

- Only one non-playable map style can be used per map.

- Judging will start then and be done for 1st April (or else heads will roll)

Quote: Map Description

[What you please]

Judging

- Me
- Resistance (Motocrosser)
- 29403

Backup (To rate judges' maps) - jbaker

Quote: Judging Criteria
O (Originality) - Were the two level types mixed an original idea? Or was it something recycled such as Race/Action or boring such as two types of puzzles? [/10]
Q (Quality) - Were the two level types merged well? Or does the contrast make you feel ill? [/10]
F (Fun Factor) - Is it a great laugh to play? Or do things such as insane easiness or difficulty or repetitiveness hinder it? [/10]
R (Replay Value) - Wannanothergo? [/10]
N (NUMA Rating) - What'd you rate it on NUMA? 4 marks for every whole Ninja, 2 for a half, ergo [/20]

Total: 39/50

The rest of my familly thought "what a twazzok". Art is subjective.

The issue I have with 'modern art' is that it comes across as pretentious: something only counts as 'art' because it was created by an 'artist'. I, currently, have three newly-wrapped Christmas presents piled on top of each other in my room. I could place those in an empty room and say it was 'a statement on how the the spiritual aspect of christmas has been lost amongst commercialism, with the gaudy colors of the gifts only highlighting the bareness of the surrounding environment' and it would be completely ignored, but if I was an established artist and it caught the public eye I could be paid disproportionate amounts of money for my 'work'.
You're right. Art is gradually turning into:

*Artist enters room*
*Artist spies bench*
*Artist turns bench upside down*
*Artist aligns bench at jaunty angle*
*Artist takes a break, grabs a cup of tea and a KitKat*
*Artist returns, and attempts to justify what on Earth he did that for*

#400861 66 2008-01-14T22:01:16Z Ad
A man walks into a bar, and half his head is an orange.

He sits down, orders a drink. The bartender eyes him warily, but gets him what he wants. The man sits sipping the drink, idly watching the soccer game on the bar television. After a while, he runs dry and orders another.

"Tell you what," says the bartender, "this next one's on the house -- but you've got to tell me what happened to your head. I don't mean to be rude there, but..."

The man smiles. "No, not at all. I get this all the time.

Well, it started with the Gulf War. I was a young kid fresh out of high school, but I was poor. I needed money for college, and the Army looked like a good way out of the ghetto. But then they shipped me over to Kuwait. My platoon took some heavy fire during Desert Storm, and I was separated from them.

I wandered the desert for days, with only the contents of my pack to sustain me. I ran out of water, I ran out of food. I was desperate, on the virge of death -- when suddenly, I saw a glint of metal in the distance...

I forced myself onward, hoping the shining brightness was a glint of gunmetal from my platoon, or a city on the horizon, or anything. When I finally reached it, it was a piece of metal half-burried in the sand. I dug around it and excavated what appeared to be an old Persian oil lamp.

There was an inscription on the lamp, too covered in dust to read. I rubbed at the embossed lettering -- and then, a swirl of smoke and light surrounded me. Suddenly, before me, stood a ten-foot tall being, dressed in traditional Arabian garb, arms crossed.

'I am the Djinni of the lamp,' said the entity. 'For releasing me, I shall grant you three wishes. What is your first wish, my master?'

I was incredulous, of course. I deduced I must be hallucinating, that this was desert madness. I decided to test the mirage. 'Alright,' I tasked it, 'I wish for a wallet with a million dollars in it, that I can never lose, and whenever I take any money out of it the sum is immediately replenished.'

'Your wish is granted!' boomed the Djinni. I felt a bluge in one of my uniform pockets. Reaching in, I pulled out a new wallet, stuffed to bursting with crisp, new American bills. I counted them -- sure enough, it was a million dollars. I ripped up the bills, cast them to the four winds, and threw the wallet as hard as I could. The moment it was beyond my sight, it teleported instantaneously back to my pocket, refilled with another million dollars.

'What is you second wish, my master?'

I pondered the notion for a long moment, assessing my needs. 'Djinni,' I said, 'for my second wish, I want to be transported to a cool, abandoned palace, into a harem room with a hundred beautiful young virgins who will all fall madly in love with me at first sight, before a buffet table set with a feast fit for a king.'

'Your wish is granted!' Poof! I found myself in a royal harem, escaped from the heat of the desert. All around me, nubile girls eyed me with keen interest. In front of me, every conceivable type of meat was roasted to perfect tenderness, set with all the appetizers, side-dishes, salads, soups, and desserts of the four corners of the globe.

I dined until I was near-bloated, and then I had a lot of sex. I mean a lot. Several hours later, laying upon a bed of feathers, brown and blonde and red haired beauties nuzzling into me like puppies at their mother's underbelly, the Djinni stood before me, looking down in satisfaction at his work so far.

'What is your third wish, my master?'

I thought long and hard. Truly, this last wish tasked the very limits of my imagination, my beliefs, my ethics, my philosophy. Hours passed in silence, save for the gentle snoring of the ladies surrounding me.

At last, I spoke.

'Djinni, for my third wish, I want half my head to be an orange.'"

Yo.

OMIGOD 1000 POSTS AND BEEN HERE 2 YEARS BOTH ON SAME DAY FEST

Here lies a map pack, that is unusual, to say the least.
The contents are weird in several ways.
The maps be all races, not usual in shape or size, style or other. Abstract to say the least.
Maps range from 400 to 3000 frames in length, with the average being approximately 800 frames.
After all, you can't play 50 long maps without killing yourself.
Secondly, you'll notice that the pack is episodic. Difficulty increases, mayhem increases. 1 column in total.
Puzzley themes are common in the latter. Thought it'd make a change. Some re-occuring themes, like forts, and the sub500 possibilities of all levels in episode 4, are fun to spot.
Thirdly, you'll notice 9 out of 50 of the maps do not currently exist. Through no fault of my own, these find themselves trapped in a dodgy hard drive. Bah. The pack should be fully up and running by the weekendend though.

Maps in this pack have had a variety of time schedules spent on them, from 10 minutes to 10 hours.
You'll be surprised how long some took.
These are a variety of my race maps, tweaked versions of those submitted to NUMA, or lurking on my computer, or brand spanking new, or otherwise, that I have finally got off my fat arse and compiled.

There's bound to be one you enjoy, so enter with an open mind.

I'd like to dedicate this pack to Epigone. For a while, I've been on the case of making... different races, but Epi brought the sh!t mainstream, and now we're seeing a great selection of abstract and original races, getting off of the current loopy loopy drone busting mainstream, which is fantastic. Mwah.

Have fun!

#19444 1 2008-03-09T12:30:26Z Ad
Why wasn't there a thread for this already? This is Mario Kart Wii, guys. Mario. Kart. Wii. You can't not love it these games. Even the shoddy Double Dash!! was awesome. And the game comes out just a few weeks from now. If you're not excited for this game, either you will be after this thread, or there may be something wrong with you. Prepare yourself.

Also, if you have any questions about the game, go ask someone in the know.

Warning: Thread may contain spoilers: screenshots, impressions, linked videos, etc.

The Basics
Quote: Wikipedia; with some edits
Like Mario Kart DS, Mario Kart Wii is based around single driver gameplay, unlike the approach by Mario Kart: Double Dash!! on the Nintendo GameCube, which featured two players on one kart.

A total of four different control choices have been confirmed. Players can choose to play the game using the Wii Wheel peripheral that comes packaged with the game, with which you tilt the control as if it were a steering wheel (although this also works without prepriheral), the remote and nunchuk, a Nintendo GameCube controller, or a Wii Classic Controller. Powersliding, another main game element, can also be set to happen automatically, to help newer drivers, but no boost will be gained.

This game has been announced as supporting the Nintendo Wi-Fi Connection service. It will support an online racing mode where players will be able to go against each other in a single race racing simultaneously and an online battle mode. It has been confirmed that it will also feature 12 player online races, and 8 player online battles. It has also been confirmed that there will be online leagues and rankings along with local rankings. Most of the online ranking will be done from a whole separate channel. You will also be able to download and send ghost data using the Nintendo Wi-Fi Connection.

Nintendo's UK site confirms that the European release of game will feature online pre-determined text chat between players before races. It will also feature an online spectator option which allows you to view your friends races and join in at the start of the next course. There will also special worldwide online events organized by Nintendo.

The game will feature many of the old weapons and items that have been used in past Mario Kart games, and that a number of new items are also being added.

In addition to expanded gameplay, motorbikes were added. In 50cc mode, karts are used; in 100cc mode, bikes are used; and in 150cc mode, players can choose between the two. In addition, you can now perform tricks in the air by shaking motion sensitive controls, or via a button on the Classic and GCN controllers. The game will also have 16 brand new tracks, and 16 remakes of older tracks, which was also incorporated into Mario Kart DS. 10 battle stages are also being added for a revamped battle mode. Miis (which can wear 3 different costumes) will also be usable during the game, along with 24 other playable characters.

USA: OUT NOW!

Spoiler: [bWeapons[/b]]Here's the item line up for this time around:

Mushrooms: Give you a boost!
Triple Mushrooms: 3 lots of the above! Use one now, and store for later?
Golden Mushroom: You're failing, but you can use this mushroom a bajillion times in about 5 seconds. GO
Mega Mushroom: Bigger is better. Apparently. Go squash stuff.
Fake Item Box: You may think it's your source of items, until you get booted in the nuts.
Banana: GO TOILET HUMOR POWER. Drop it or throw it forward and watch'em slide.
Triple Bananas: They follow you, until you deploy them. Good for shielding yourself from attack.
Green Shell: Line up, shoot, laugh, stop paying attention, crash, lose.
Triple Green Shells: Swirl around you until you use them. Same old, same old.
Red Shell: As the games progress their aim increases. Shoot at a wall from point blank and you'll most likely hit someone.
Triple Red Shells: Triple the homing-y goodness!
Blue Shell: If you're any good, you'll despise this first place mangler.
Star: Restores power to the observatory. And makes you LETHALLY INVINCIBLE
Thunderbolt: You're in last place, and apparently making everyone small helps you.
Thundercloud: The arcade games sucked ass, didn't they? This thing hates you. Pass it on by crashing into Luigi.
Bob-omb: Lob it or drop it, its on a timer. Get outta there!
Blooper: It splodges on everyone infront of you, destroying a player's vision and making CPU swerve.
Bullet Bill: Carries you forward. Hang back at the beginning of a race, get it, reclaim first, and use it to extend your lead.
POW Block: Fed up of Crash stealing their racing ideas, Mario de-Aussies a TNT. Suck that, bandicoot.

#441024 28 2008-06-01T08:50:18Z Ad
Hm... I got mine last year (way before free United Forever upgrade) for 10/$20 on Play.com.
That's ridiculously cheap for a game over here, seeing as it retailed at 29.99, the price of a DS game, so maybe have a shop around for the old version, if you don't want a pair of 3D specs, and are willing to download a gigabyte of game.

As for the game, it's a classic. Stadium is unusual in terms of environment, the others are more realistic, and scenery-based, with far more pieces (they've added the whole walled flats section and better terraformers. All the cars control extremely differently, with Island being full throttle, Coast being extreme realism, and snow being almost comedic, with perfect traction on land and none off-road, you'll find some you like even more than Stadium. Although Stadium is pretty cool. lus, all other locations hardly ever lag.

Racing is not the only thing you can do: stunt maps (with a Tony Hawk's feel), platform maps (where you get a point penalty every time you fall off), and puzzles (where you get half a course and an array of pieces, and you've got to find the best combination) mean there's plenty of variety. Plus more mods than you could shake a stick at. And everything's so pretty... Not that I'd know, I'm on a 6 year old Dell with a Celeron and 256mb RAM _

Anyhow, ME LAMP TRACKMANIAAA, so hopefully you will too. Plus the servers are emptier. So less lag for me!

EDIT: Hah, Play've put the price up to 24.99 due to the arrival of Forever. That's 2.5x the price!
Although I tapped it into Google, and I found it for $34.99.

EDIT EDIT: 14.99 at Game, 4.99 brand new on Ebay.
Hmm, I can only find it on UK price comparison sites... odd.

EDIT EDIT EDIT: APPARENTLY it's $20 on Steam. Not that I have Steam.

EDIT YADA: You don't have Manialinks?! Well, it's like an in-game Internet browser for all your trackmania needs - skins, new car models, tracks, mods, etc.

#467597 44 2008-09-06T15:50:22Z Ad
While N+ for DS has its flaws
Spoiler: *Ahem*SETTINGS:
- No settings saved
- Blood non-existent

MENUS:
- Overlapping songs
- Crazy map number arrangement
- Crazier unlockable map number arrangement
- Show us the actual maps on the level select menu, not just the tiles!

GAMEPLAY:
- Jump into a ceiling tile spike, and you go down and then back up again!
- You won! But everything can still kill you though. Well, except zap drones. They're picky.
- Chaingun drones are used... once? In a custom map, methinks. Object variety is a bit poor.
- Bounce block drones, and all their flaws.
- There's only 262 levels! It took me a total of 5 hours to complete.
- Chaser drones can pick up the ninja when he's not in the same column/row. This results in the things trying to attack you through walls. This is most apparent in the tutorial level.
- Difficulty shmifficulty. Until you get the Atari Bonus. Then you just get slapped hard.
- X = suicide. X = main menu. Ad = kepp trying to commit suicide just before dying, but not quite fast enough. Ad = furious at having to do episode 35 seven times, and episode 49 three times because of this. Grr.

AESTHETICS:
- Despite the low-memory visuals, there's still a POP affect as new objects scroll onto the screen.
- There's a red tint as you start a level, which can make lasers invisible. A bummer, to say the least.
- Alternate colour ninjas are proud hosts of ugly outlines...
- None of the objects are lined up accurately. Especially one ways.
- Pure rockets have some form of orange rectangle following them.
- Pure drones are not exactly octagonal, and the eyes of the zap drones are like different entities: they pass over things that the drone does not, and turn ridiculously slowly.
- Wassat, at the bottom right of the top screen? When you're selecting a level? See it? It's having a spasm. Click L & R to see the renegade pixels!
Backwards sliding down bounce blocks!

LEVEL EDITOR:
- F*cking ridiculous to use if you're left handed.
- You can delete the outer walls! FAIL
- Thwumps often do not work
- Help is not helpful. AT ALL.
- What's with all the useless tiles? Boo.
- Toggle on/Toggle off?
- Colours?
- The "tools L help R" bar needs to sod off and die.

UNLOCKABLES:
- Music 2. 20000 gold. By completing all 262 levels, I collected 10000 gold. I have to play them all again?
- Atari bonus. Don't see how it's Atari's bonus, these are N levels! But yeah, it requires a code. Any reason? Seems like a useless addition, just give us the episodes for completing the other 45.

ONLINE & MULITPLAYER:
-Coming soon!

BOX:
- It's American. It's odd.
- The ninja's ultimate goal is to achieve transcendence. Gold cannot be a goal. Gold is an object. And another thing, "gold" is stretched.
- "You are a ninja". Catchy!
- Why write about the level editor first? The penultimate bullet point should be first.
- Y'know what? Scrub the bullet points, use paragraphs. Look at the last one. "Outwit stuff and run fast"
- "N," is not a thing. Also, there's another comma missing after "N+".
New! - "Enemiesas" and "theultimate" are not words.
New! - Not sure about this, but should it not be "...to test others' ninja skills", as opposed to "other's"?

REPLAYS:
- Never seem to work first time.
- Close your DS midway through, and a baddie might get you, even if you won.
- Commit suicide, now run the demo. Just wait for nothing to happen. Fuuunnn.

CREDITS:
- "N N N N N!"
- "'The Oracle'"? "'Bug Slayer'"? "G-Lo"? I doubt these people are as cool as they think they are.

GENERAL STUPIDITY:
- Timed mines have been invented, but they're only used in a tutorial
- Inertia?! Oh dear. And that's not used at all.
- 8 spaces to save offline content. Not even 8 spaces to save offline maps.
Replays too. And I've just covered how crap they are.

If I've missed anything, I apologize.
I enjoyed my playthrough thoroughly.
...Seriously.

edit: (New Additions in BOX)

#468490 212 2008-09-09T20:52:31Z Ad
Hmm... with NReality v7.0 on the horizon, I noticed some sections have become a bit scruffy with all the additions. Not to fear! I am in the process of making some new screen mock-ups, in which I'm rearranging and reorganizing quite a few of the additions. Although I would love to see these implemented, they're merely suggestions that we (Unreality ) should try and neaten NReality up a bit before the next major release, and maybe include a few more helpful areas.

So far, I've redone the main menu and the userlevels page. There's minimal stuff done to the main menu, but I have included a whole host of new features within the userlevels page: the ability to run a NUMA search, the inclusion of your NUMA favourites, and the Hot Maps list, to name the major ones. Also, there's specific help on each section to the left of the screen.
Obviously, I'm no coder, I have no idea how long these ideas would take - or if they're even possible - I just thought them up whilst I was fiddling with NReality in Paint, and decided to include them, to see what everyone else thought of them.

Hmm... how to display them all...

NReality loads in n_v14.swf and changes the functions inside.
